label: Paradox, Mechanism, Reframe
line: Two true facts about a thing the viewer owns that cannot both be true. Give the answer in one line early, show how it works, and end by turning the opening belief upside down.
best_for: a thing the viewer owns or uses every day works in a way that seems impossible
a business or a system does something that looks like a loss and is not
also_for: a mechanism in the viewer's own body or habits
avoid_for: an object the viewer has never held or wondered about
a topic with no paradox the viewer has felt: a definition with a 'but' added is not one
signals: the viewer has held or used the thing
two facts about it seem unable to both be true
the explanation is a mechanism of four to six steps
the answer changes how the viewer sees the thing

beats.name: Paradox
beats.job: Two facts about the viewer's own object that seem incompatible, in one sentence.

beats.name: Question and one-line answer
beats.job: Ask what it is really doing and answer in one line: not the thing the viewer assumed, this other thing. The what is given; the how is held back.

beats.name: Scene that will fail
beats.job: One everyday scene with the viewer in it, which the mechanism will break later.

beats.name: Mechanism
beats.job: Four to six steps, one concrete noun in each. One real number or name in the whole script.

beats.name: Turn
beats.job: 'But': the scene from the third beat fails, and the mechanism is the reason.

beats.name: That is also why
beats.job: Two more things the viewer has lived through that the same mechanism explains.

beats.name: Reframe
beats.job: Turn the opening belief upside down in two sentences, then stop.

hooks.shape: [Your thing] [does surprising A], and [fails at obvious B].
[Every part of it] is [a handicap], and it still [works] almost every time. So how?
[Organisation or system] [does something that looks like throwing value away], every day.

holds: Two questions are open inside the first fifth: the paradox, and a scene that has not failed yet. Because the answer arrives early, the viewer stays for the how. The question re-opens at the scene, at the turn and at the first 'also why'.
ending: The reframe: the belief the paradox planted, stated the other way round as a fact. No recap of the mechanism and no lesson.
first_frame: The paradox drawn literally, both facts on screen at once: the thing that works where it should not, beside the thing that fails where it should work.
pitfalls: Naming the mechanism's technical term before the viewer has seen it work
Ending on a summary of the mechanism where the turned-around belief belongs
template: [Thing you own] [does surprising A], and [ignores obvious B]. So what is it doing? It is not [what you assumed], it is [the real mechanism, one line]. Picture [an everyday scene that will fail]. [Step]. [Step]. [Step]. [Step]. But [the scene fails], so [consequence]. That is also why [something you have lived]. And why [a second one]. So [your thing] never [what you assumed]. It [the real mechanism].
